4-compute-the-full-file-hash-only-when-a.line: For a new file the full SHA-256 is most of its duplicate check and is never needed, and most imported files are new. Not yet judged.

why.impact: Removes the largest step of the check for every new file.
why.odds: Idea 1 shows the full-hash passes dominate the check, so skipping one is almost sure to show.
why.path: Changes what idea 2 can still save, so it goes before it.

5-store-each-picture-s-full-file-hash-so.line: Re-reading the library copy is about half of a duplicate's 4.2 ms, and this removes it. Not yet judged.

why.impact: Idea 1 puts 88-91% of a duplicate's cost in two full-hash passes, one of which this deletes.
why.odds: Needs a migration and a guard against a file changed after its hash was stored.

6-hash-the-staged-import-s-files-in-para.line: Hashing is now known to be the check's main cost, so overlapping it across files matters more than first thought. Not yet judged.

why.impact: Shortens the hashing that dominates a duplicate's check, but it overlaps ideas 4 and 5.
why.odds: Depends on the disk; the gain may shrink once 4 and 5 remove passes.
why.path: Best judged after 4 and 5 show what hashing is left.

2-read-each-incoming-file-once-for-the-s.line: After idea 4, little repeat reading is left inside the check; the rest is picture creation, outside the question. Not yet judged.

why.impact: The sampled hash reads only about 64 KiB, and the remaining extra read belongs to picture creation, which is dominated by decoding.
why.odds: Warm page cache already makes repeat reads cheap.
why.path: Its saving depends on what idea 4 leaves.

3-look-up-all-of-a-batch-s-files-in-one-.line: The lookup measured 0.3 ms on an idle writer, too small to matter unless a busy server makes it wait. Not yet judged.

why.impact: 0.3 ms of a 4.2 ms duplicate and almost none of a new file's 145 ms.
why.odds: Only a long queue on a busy writer thread would make batching pay, and that is unmeasured.
why.path: Idea 1's suggested follow-up, timing the lookup on a busy server, would settle whether this is worth doing.
